minutes.headline: Board ratified a new land use director, named a conservation member, and warned On the Rocks over after-hours drinking.
minutes.summary: The Select Board, joined by the Planning Board, ratified the town manager's land use director appointment. It then interviewed three conservation commission candidates and appointed one on a split vote. It held a liquor license hearing ending in a written warning, allowed early Sunday hours for one event, heard an electric aggregation update on rising winter rates, and heard a resident's concern about a school-area crosswalk.

public_comment.topic: Lions club representatives asked residents for grocery gift cards or checks to restock the food pantry and described the Thanksgiving basket drive.
A resident raised safety of the crosswalk at Main, Highland and Oak streets with added construction and school traffic, and asked for a town plan.

what_happened.line: The Select Board warned JK Waterfront, doing business as On the Rocks, and required employee training after a liquor license hearing; the vote was not audible.
The board directed the town manager to send all license holders a reminder of local regulations.
The board appointed Thomas Bertram to the conservation commission on a split vote, with one member opposed.
Joined by the Planning Board, the board ratified the town manager's land use director appointment; the vote was not audible.
The board approved an 8 am Sunday opening for Embers Pizzeria for one day only and asked for a letter on its requested hours.

why_it_matters: The warning and the regulations reminder affect how local liquor licenses are enforced, and a repeat violation could bring stronger penalties for license holders.
The electric aggregation consultant said winter utility rates will rise sharply, which bears on household electric bills and on whether the town locks in a fixed-rate contract.
The crosswalk safety concern and the possible ADA bylaw amendment could lead to traffic spending and a vote at the fall town meeting.
watch_next: A package of crosswalk and traffic measures from the town manager, after consulting the police chief and DPW director.
A possible ADA bylaw amendment at the fall town meeting, and a later agenda item on Embers' requested hours once its letter is submitted.

reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the main motions: Bertram's appointment, the warning to On the Rocks, the reminder letter and Embers' 8 am hours. They differ on follow-up actions and figures. Ours has no tallies or names for several votes, such as the cable committee. The warrant figures were partly garbled by the captions, but the aggregation rates and the ADA and crosswalk follow-ups are described differently, so check the recording.
